These could be assembled into a policy-scoped card for an agent. Nothing in the evidence frames this as an AI-agent use case, and merchant locks, amount caps and expiry are not explicitly named as rule types. missing for 10: vendor documentation of the agent/AI use case by name, explicit merchant-lock and amount-cap rule documentation, configurable card expiry, independent or hands-on corroboration.

The docs show API-driven card operations: creating virtual and physical cards as paymentInstrument resources, updating cards via /paymentInstruments/{id}, and activating, suspending or closing them. Transaction rules provide spend controls, per-card balances exist, and webhooks report balance and payment events, so an agent could plausibly drive the core program through the API. However, transaction viewing is shown only in the Customer Area UI, relayed-authorisation setup is a Customer Area step, and nothing shows an MCP surface or scoped, least-privilege agent credentials (only an llms.txt exists; OpenAPI probes returned 404). Missing for 10: an MCP server or agent-specific surface, scoped API credential/permission documentation, an evidenced API for reading balances and transactions, a discoverable OpenAPI spec, and independent hands-on corroboration.
